item.title: Entanglement Enhanced Sensing with Qubits affected by non-Markovian Dephasing
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Noah Kaufmann, Kasper H. Nielsen, Eva M. González-Ruiz, Anders S. Sørensen
arXiv:2604.22368v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement has been proposed as a means to improve the sensitivity of sensing weak signals. While the degree of this quantum advantage is well understood in noiseless settings, the situation is more complex under realistic conditions, where the system is subject to decoherence. In this case, the enhancement depends on the specific noise characteristics. Previous treatments of colored noise typically assume that the noise is uncorrelated between successive experiments. Here, we consider the scenario in which the noise exhibits correlations across multiple shots. We derive a simple fundamental limit to the sensitivity based on the fact that the sensitivity cannot be better than the signal-to-noise ratio seen by the probe. Focusing on Ram…

item.description:

👤 Yukun Yang, Ranjani G. Sundaram, Himanshu Gupta
arXiv:2610.26099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributing quantum circuits across a network of quantum devices is a recent approach to improve the scalability of quantum computation. Entangled pairs of qubits distributed across network nodes are used as a communication resource for executing inter-node (remote) gates. However, establishing these entanglement pairs incurs significant latency, and doing so during the circuit's execution may lead to the decoherence of logical qubits. Instead, it may be beneficial to distribute certain entanglement pairs before the circuit is executed. Thus, we consider the problem of distributing a quantum circuit across a quantum network containing some pre-distributed entanglement pairs and seek to minimize the execution time of the circuit. arXiv:2509.03288v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a symmetry-enabled direct quantum protocol for computing many-body Green's functions, a central tool for studying strongly correlated quantum systems. Total-spin conservation then fixes the otherwise inaccessible intersite fluctuation, converting two local spectra into a bound on a collective entanglement witness. arXiv:2605.16944v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum adiabatic algorithm for solving MIS with Rydberg atoms, which uses graph degrees to engineer the Hamiltonian for adiabatic evolution. Our approach extends the algorithm of Pichler et al. for MIS state preparation, which uses time-dependent global controls to excite atoms while the Rydberg blockade mechanism suppresses adjacent excitations. 👤 Yuanxing Hao, Marin Bukov
arXiv:2610.24039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For given control channels, quantum control theory determines whether quantum gates can be realized, but not their resilience to errors. We address this problem by establishing existence criteria for robust gate implementation in d-level systems. Our criteria reveal that implementability of all gates is not enough: a universal family of robust gates exists if and only if the driven Hamiltonians share no common symmetry. When these criteria hold, we can make gates resilient to any combination of static perturbations, uniform Hamiltonian rescaling, perturbations at a finite set of selected frequencies, and perturbations with arbitrary selected waveforms. 👤 Noah Kaufmann, Anders Søndberg Sørensen
arXiv:2610.25912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of entanglement in sensing is often motivated by improved sensitivity arising from non-classical correlations among probes. For static signals, however, this quantum advantage in Ramsey spectroscopy with N probes is known to be highly susceptible to dephasing, which severely limits the possible gain from entanglement. In contrast, we consider sensing of signals that vary in time. Considering the simplest example of dephasing by classical white noise, we show that entanglement allows a large increase in bandwidth when estimating the frequency components of a time-dependent signal. Without sacrificing any sensitivity, entanglement allows for an increase in bandwidth by a factor of N. Alternatively, when interrogation times are limited…

item.title: Gradient-Based Optimization Enables Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Gate Synthesis
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Marc Grau Davis, Ed Younis, Mathias Weiden, Hyeongrak Choi, Dirk Englund
arXiv:2603.25101v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a numerical approach to optimizing a quantum circuit over a discrete gate set by using gradient descent to tune R_Z angles to a solution where many R_Z gates can be rounded to a Clifford or T gate without introducing further synthesis error. Through benchmarking, we show that our approach is able to match state-of-the-art techniques for multi-qubit Clifford + T circuit synthesis, and is able to find circuits for unitaries that previous approaches fail to find solutions for. Our approach can adapt to any discrete gate set, which we demonstrate using the Clifford + T + sqrt T gate set.

arXiv:2610.26120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum communication networks promise information-theoretic security but this security collapses if intermediate relay nodes are compromised, a risk that grows sharply when compromised nodes cannot be identified. arXiv:2610.24160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Trajectree, a quantum trajectory-based quantum circuit simulator that uses a novel, state-saving partial execution of the quantum circuits to simulate broad and deep noisy quantum circuits efficiently. This creates a fundamentally online problem: the system must react to stochastic arrivals, balance latency and throughput, and remain stable under varying loads without foresight of future jobs. item.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Xiao-Kan Guo
arXiv:2604.27328v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. We first give a self-contained derivation of the Fokker--Planck equation that governs the time evolution of the mixing measure for a Gaussian mixture. Then, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture to study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.

arXiv:2610.25894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum states are ultimately responsible for numerous counterintuitive phenomena that defy classical intuition. As the development of quantum technologies accelerates, our ability to harness these quantum resources becomes essential. This review addresses a fundamental question. How do we quantify the quantumness of a state, and which specific traits distinguish it from its classical counterparts? We examine quantumness through both theoretical and operational lenses, providing a clear framework for state characterization. Ultimately, we demonstrate that certifying quantumness is not just a theoretical exercise. It is a practical necessity for identifying, and realizing quantum advantage in real-world applications.
